topic: Trains - locomotive sanders (sand on the rails for grip)
question: WHAT IS IT BLASTING
ONTO THE RAILS?
answer_full: Sand, for more grip – the system is called a sander
recap: A heavy freight locomotive couldn't pull away on wet rails, until small pipes blasted a brownish jet right in front of its wheels.
explain: Wet rails and fallen leaves make the steel slippery. So the driving wheels just spin, instead of pulling the train.
So the locomotive uses compressed air to blow dry sand through small pipes, right between the wheel and the rail.
The hard grains get crushed under the wheel and give it something to bite on. That's why a modern locomotive carries hundreds of kilos of sand on board.
